      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

It has been oversold and won’t stop the decline in North Sea jobs, as it will be largely unmanned and operated remotely.</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/21/jackdaw-gasfield-labour-andy-burnham-zack-polanski-uk-politics-latest-news">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Billionaire Michael Bloomberg is spending $80m to help Democratic candidates, while Trump has promised Republicans $400m. Plus a vital investigation into justice in Louisiana</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2018/sep/17/guardian-us-morning-briefing-sign-up-to-stay-informed"><strong>Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>Good morning. Vast sums of money are being <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/michael-bloomberg-donation-democrats-midterms">ploughed into November’s midterms</a>, with the billionaire Michael Bloomberg spending $80m to help Democratic candidates, and Donald Trump announcing he intends to spend $400m to aid Republican candidates, with $300m already disbursed.</p><p>Bloomberg made the contributions in September and October, particularly focused on Democrats running to flip the US House of Representatives. Democrats believe they are favored to take back the House, though they’ve acknowledged trailing Republicans in fundraising. Republicans are also being aided by the president’s ally Elon Musk, who has spent $366m so far.</p><p><strong>What are the main issues for voters in the midterms?</strong> In <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2026/oct/20/voter-issues-midterms-elections">this explainer</a>, Robert Tait looks at six key issues swaying how people might vote – the economy, Iran, immigration, Trump’s use of power, AI and datacenters and the state of democracy and voter rights in the US.</p><p><strong>What is happening between the DoJ and California over voter rolls?</strong> The justice department’s list of suspected noncitizens in California includes a “high percentage” of people born in the US, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/doj-non-citizens-la">Los Angeles election officials said</a>. The statement, made in court papers, raises further questions about the reliability of the list of 20,000 people the DoJ is demanding be investigated.</p><p><strong>What was strange about how the ADL reminded people about an antisemitic slur? </strong>The Anti-Defamation League ADL has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/trump-kansas-rally-antisemitic-slur-anti-defamation-league">denounced the use of the term “shylock”</a> as antisemitic, without explaining that the slur had been used a day earlier by Trump in a speech in Kansas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/first-thing-midterms-spending-money-donations-michael-bloomberg">Continue reading...</a></description>
